front_blocks.md: Define the term **burette**.

back_blocks.md: A **burette** is a piece of apparatus used to measure a variable volume of liquid between 0 cm<sup>3</sup> and 50 cm<sup>3</sup>. It is the most accurate way to measure variable volumes and is read from top to bottom (0.00 cm<sup>3</sup> at the top).

cards.back_md: A **burette** is a piece of apparatus used to measure a variable volume of liquid between 0 cm<sup>3</sup> and 50 cm<sup>3</sup>. It is the most accurate way to measure variable volumes and is read from top to bottom (0.00 cm<sup>3</sup> at the top).

front_blocks.md: Why is a gas syringe preferred over downward displacement of water for collecting gas?

back_blocks.md: A **gas syringe** is preferred because it is more precise and accurate. Downward displacement of water cannot be used if the gas is **soluble** in water, which would give an inaccurate volume reading.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A digital balance should be tared before use.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Taring** sets the balance to zero before use, ensuring the mass reading reflects only the substance being weighed and not the container.

front_blocks.md: What is the correct unit of **temperature** in chemistry experiments?

back_blocks.md: Temperature is measured in **degrees Celsius (°C)**. Laboratory thermometers typically have a precision of 0.5 °C or 1 °C, while digital temperature probes can read to 0.1 °C.

front_blocks.md: Define **downward displacement of water** as a gas collection method.

back_blocks.md: **Downward displacement of water** is a method of collecting gas where an inverted measuring cylinder filled with water captures the gas produced. It cannot be used for gases that are soluble in water.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A stopwatch display reading 1:30 should be recorded as 1.30 minutes.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A display of 1:30 means 1 minute and 30 seconds, which is **1.5 minutes** or **90 seconds**. Recording it as 1.30 minutes is a common error.

front_blocks.md: Which piece of apparatus is most accurate for measuring a **variable** volume of liquid?

front_blocks.md: Why is the **pencil line** kept above the solvent level at the start of a chromatography experiment involving liquid volume measurement?

back_blocks.md: The pencil line must be above the solvent level so that the sample spots do not dissolve directly into the solvent. This ensures the solvent carries the substances up the paper by **capillary action** rather than washing them away.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **solvent**.

back_blocks.md: A **solvent** is the liquid in which a solute dissolves to form a solution. For example, water is the solvent in seawater.

cards.back_md: A **solvent** is the liquid in which a solute dissolves to form a solution. For example, water is the solvent in seawater.

front_blocks.md: When sugar dissolves in tea, what is the sugar called?

back_blocks.md: The sugar is called the **solute**. A **solute** is the substance that dissolves in a solvent to form a solution.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A solution can contain only one solute.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A solution may contain **more than one** solute dissolved in the same solvent. Seawater, for example, contains several different dissolved salts.

front_blocks.md: A **solution** is a mixture of one or more **..........**  dissolved in a **solvent**; the substance left behind after filtration is called the **..........** .

back_blocks.md: A **solution** is a mixture of one or more **solutes** dissolved in a **solvent**; the substance left behind after filtration is called the **residue**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between the **filtrate** and the **residue** in a filtration?

back_blocks.md: The **filtrate** is the liquid or solution that passes through the filter paper. The **residue** is the solid that remains on the filter paper and does not pass through.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **saturated solution**.

back_blocks.md: A **saturated solution** is a solution containing the maximum concentration of solute dissolved in the solvent at a specified temperature. Adding more solute will not cause further dissolution.

cards.back_md: A **saturated solution** is a solution containing the maximum concentration of solute dissolved in the solvent at a specified temperature. Adding more solute will not cause further dissolution.

front_blocks.md: Why does a substance described as **insoluble** not form a solution?

back_blocks.md: An **insoluble** substance will not dissolve in a given solvent. Its particles do not break apart and mix evenly with the solvent particles, so no solution is formed. For example, sand is insoluble in water.

cards.front_md: Why does a substance described as **insoluble** not form a solution?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The filtrate is always a pure substance.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **filtrate** is the liquid or solution that passes through the filter. It may still contain dissolved substances and is not necessarily pure — it is only free of undissolved solids.

front_blocks.md: When copper(II) sulfate crystals are stirred into water, the crystals are the **..........**, the water is the **..........**, and the blue liquid formed is the **..........**.
